brief.headline: Patch Claude Code now: worktree escape and hook bypass fixed
brief.summary:
Claude Code 2.1.222 closes two holes that hit directly at the worktree-plus-hooks setup you run overnight: worktree-isolated sessions and subagents could run destructive git against your main checkout, and a PreToolUse hook could be bypassed inside background agent tasks. Update before your next unattended run — this is exactly the failure mode that turns "describe the work, go to sleep" into a damaged main branch.

On the verification side, fable-method and fablize both package the same "think / act / prove" idea into portable skills/plugins that force a completion-and-evidence check before an agent calls a task done — worth wiring in as your morning-PR trust gate. On cost, opencodex and claude-code-router (now on v3.0.19, with fixed provider routing and accurate model logging) let you point background subagents at local or cheap models like DeepSeek or Ollama without leaving your existing harness, and devspace lets you burn a ChatGPT/Claude web login instead of metered API tokens for background coding work. dao-code adds cache-reusing forks so long DeepSeek-V4 sessions don't re-pay full context every turn.
bullets: Update Claude Code to 2.1.222 — fixes worktree-isolated agents running destructive git on your main checkout and a PreToolUse hook bypass in background tasks
Drop fable-method or the fablize plugin into your setup as a think/act/prove verification gate before Opus marks a task complete
Route background subagents through opencodex or claude-code-router v3.0.19 (now logs the actual routed model) to hit local/DeepSeek/Ollama endpoints instead of paying full API rates
Try dao-code with DeepSeek-V4's cache-reusing forks for long memory-heavy overnight sessions without re-paying full context each turn
Use devspace to run background coding tasks off your existing ChatGPT/Claude web login instead of separately metered API credits
Install codeseek as an MCP server so subagents get real call-graph/semantic search instead of grep-guessing into the wrong files

signals.label: Self-verification gates on agent output
signals.note: fable-method and fablize both converge on forcing completion/evidence/verification before an agent claims done — the missing piece for trusting an overnight PR

signals.label: Cost routing to cheap/local models
signals.note: opencodex, dao-code, claude-code-router, devspace, Homebench and a wave of small open-weight releases (Shieldstral, Maple-Preview) all target moving subagent work off metered API tokens

signals.label: Unattended-run safety gaps still being found
signals.note: Claude Code 2.1.222 had to patch a worktree isolation escape and a hook bypass — the exact primitives long unattended runs depend on

signals.label: Off-desk control plane tooling
signals.note: omnigent, ongrid and LiveAgent are all early attempts at checking on or steering agents from a phone or chat app rather than a laptop UI

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.222 fixes worktree-isolated sessions/subagents being able to run destructive git commands against the main checkout, and closes a PreToolUse hook bypass in background agent tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Both bugs directly undermine the worktree-plus-hooks setup you rely on for unattended runs; the isolation escape could have let a runaway agent damage your main checkout.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code to 2.1.222 before your next unattended overnight run.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: A new open-source repo ships CLI tools — loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost — for designing and orchestrating multi-agent coding loops.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you scaffolding to structure and audit long-running agent loops instead of hand-rolling prompts, plus a built-in way to track what each loop costs.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering and run `loop-init` to scaffold a loop, then `loop-audit` before you trust it unattended.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is a universal provider proxy that lets Codex CLI and Claude Code call any LLM — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama — through one config.
items.whyItMatters: Lets him route cheap or local models into subagents inside his existing Claude Code/Codex setup without switching harnesses.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point a background subagent's model config at a local Ollama or DeepSeek endpoint tonight.

items.title: New release of LLM adds support for reasoning traces, OpenAI Responses, server-side tools, and smarter logging
items.tldr: LLM 0.32 ships visible reasoning traces (to stderr, suppress with --hide-reasoning/-R), OpenAI Responses API support, server-side provider tools, and redesigned content-addressable SQLite logging.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you watch or hide a reasoning model's chain-of-thought from the CLI and get structured, queryable logs of every call for post-mortems on unattended runs.
items.tryThis: pip install -U llm, run a reasoning model and check stderr for traces, add --hide-reasoning/-R for clean output, and query the new SQLite log after a run.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and custom agents under one policy/sandboxing layer, controllable from any device.
items.whyItMatters: One control plane to mix harnesses and check on unattended runs from his phone instead of being locked into a single tool's UI.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and wire an existing Claude Code worktree into it to test checking on a run from your phone.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns a ChatGPT or Claude web login into a Codex/Claude-Code-style CLI agent.
items.whyItMatters: Lets him tap web-subscription usage for agent coding tasks instead of separately metered API tokens — a direct cost lever.
items.tryThis: Clone Waishnav/devspace and route a background coding task through your existing ChatGPT/Claude web login instead of API credits.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills a "think / act / prove" workflow into portable skills plus an eval, so any model self-checks its work before calling a task done.
items.whyItMatters: This is the self-verification loop needed to trust an overnight PR without babysitting it — an eval that can gate any agent's output.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and drop its skills/eval into your Claude Code setup as a post-task verification gate.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is a terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 that uses byte-stable prompt prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory adds almost no token cost.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete way to run long, memory-heavy agent sessions on a cheap model without re-paying full context every turn, and it's Claude Code config compatible.
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code, point it at DeepSeek-V4, and use its cache-fork setup for a long overnight task instead of paying full context cost each turn.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local-first desktop widget tracking token usage, cost, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
items.whyItMatters: Real visibility into what overnight agent runs actually cost across every tool, not just one CLI's own counter.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor and check per-tool spend after your next unattended overnight run.

items.title: withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit — Your AI forgets. This remembers. Spec-driven coding harness for vibecoders, product owners, CEOs and real builders — self-improving context memory, 15 agents, 33 skills working with /goal, agent-team, & work
items.tldr: vibecode-pro-max-kit is a spec-driven harness with 15 agents and 33 skills built around /goal and agent-team commands to run autopilot loops with zero human gating.
items.whyItMatters: This is the exact shape of the reader's goal — describe work, walk away — with named commands to test rather than a vague pitch.
items.tryThis: Clone withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit and run /goal on a real ticket to see how far the autopilot loop gets before needing a human gate.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: fivetaku/fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus through completion, evidence and verification checks before it can call a task done.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets getting an agent to verify its own work overnight instead of just claiming it's finished.
items.tryThis: Install the fivetaku/fablize plugin and route your overnight Opus runs through it.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI building call graphs and hybrid dense/sparse/reranked search indexes across 7 languages, shipped as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex.
items.whyItMatters: Gives agents real code navigation instead of grep-guessing, cutting the wrong-file edits and clarifying questions that break unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Install CodeBendKit/codeseek as an MCP server in your Claude Code config and have subagents query it instead of raw file search.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane that rotates overnight work across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions by quota, with shared thread context and cross-model review.
items.whyItMatters: Directly cuts cost and throttling pain by spreading long unattended runs across accounts instead of hitting one subscription's cap.
items.tryThis: Set up razzant/claudexor with your Claude/Codex subscriptions and let it round-robin an overnight run across quotas.

items.title: yan5xu/codexloom — Turn Codex threads into an organization of long-lived domain agents.
items.tldr: codexloom turns OpenAI Codex threads into an organization of long-lived, domain-specific agents.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete pattern for keeping persistent specialized subagents alive across sessions instead of re-briefing fresh context each run — same problem your worktree/subagent setup is solving.
items.tryThis: Clone yan5xu/codexloom and wire one recurring task into a long-lived domain agent instead of a one-shot session.

items.title: Show HN: Maple-Preview – Ternary 20B MoE running at 120 tok/s on a iPhone
items.tldr: Show HN: Maple-Preview runs a ternary 20B MoE model at 120 tok/s directly on an iPhone.
items.whyItMatters: You ship mobile apps — this is a concrete on-device inference speed/size data point for building offline AI features without a server round-trip.
items.tryThis: Grab the Maple-Preview Show HN demo/repo and benchmark it on your target iPhone hardware.

items.title: Agent skills that bring team coding standards to Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: A new set of agent skills packages team coding standards directly into Claude Code and Codex.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you encode your own lint/style/PR rules once so every agent run follows them without you re-prompting each time.
items.tryThis: Pull these skill files into your repo's .claude/skills (or Codex equivalent) and point them at your existing style guide.

items.title: Homebench – Benchmark local LLMs for speed, memory, and quality
items.tldr: Homebench is a new open-source benchmark for testing local LLM speed, memory footprint, and output quality on your own machine.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you empirically pick which open-weight model to route cheap or background subagent work to instead of trusting leaderboards.
items.tryThis: Clone Homebench and run it against candidate local models on your dev machine to pick a router target for cheap tasks.

items.title: v3.0.19
items.tldr: claude-code-router 3.0.19 fixes a Codex provider 404 routing bug, makes API key comparison constant-time, and now shows the actual routed model in request logs.
items.whyItMatters: If you tier subagents across providers through this router, the constant-time key check closes a timing side-channel and the log fix stops you misdiagnosing which model actually ran a task.
items.tryThis: Upgrade claude-code-router to v3.0.19 now.

items.title: llm-anthropic 0.26
items.tldr: llm-anthropic 0.26 adds claude-fable-5/sonnet-5/opus-5 and replaces ad-hoc web-search flags with a unified -T tool interface (WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, AnthropicMCP).
items.whyItMatters: Gives you server-side tool calls straight from the llm CLI for quick scripted checks outside your main agent harness.
items.tryThis: pip install -U llm-anthropic 'llm>=0.32', then call `llm -T WebSearch -T CodeExecution` instead of the old -o web_search flags.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: ponytail is a tool aimed at biasing your AI agent toward the smallest possible diff — 'the best code is the code you never wrote.'
items.whyItMatters: Smaller, lazier diffs are what makes an overnight PR reviewable in five minutes instead of fifty.
items.tryThis: Try DietrichGebert/ponytail as a skill/hook to nudge agents toward minimal-diff solutions before your next overnight run.

items.title: elder-plinius/T3MP3ST — autonomous red teaming platform; multi-agent offensive-security meta-harness
items.tldr: T3MP3ST is an autonomous, multi-agent red-teaming platform for offensive security testing.
items.whyItMatters: A way to have agents adversarially probe his own shipped code for security holes before merging, instead of trusting the coding agent's own say-so.
items.tryThis: Clone elder-plinius/T3MP3ST and point it at a staging build the night before review for a security pass alongside the PR.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is an open-source auth gateway giving agents authenticated access to 1000+ SaaS providers via SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP or OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: Removes a common reason overnight agent runs stall — missing credentials or tool access to the services they need mid-task.
items.tryThis: Clone oomol-lab/open-connector and wire it up as an MCP server so agents can auth into SaaS tools without asking you first.

items.title: nexu-io/html-video — Programmatic video for coding agents — HTML to video on your laptop. Turn HTML, CSS & data into real MP4s with pluggable render engines, 21 templates, AI soundtrack. Apache-2.0, no per-render fees. An official project b
items.tldr: html-video is an Apache-2.0 repo that renders HTML/CSS/data into real MP4s locally, with pluggable engines and no per-render fees.
items.whyItMatters: Lets an overnight coding agent auto-generate a walkthrough video attached to its PR, cutting the time you spend reviewing what changed in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone nexu-io/html-video and have your agent pipe a demo HTML page through it to attach an MP4 to its PR.

items.title: DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices — Provider-neutral Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code, and agentic harness design.
items.tldr: agents-best-practices packages provider-neutral guidance for designing Codex/Claude Code agent skills and harnesses as an installable Agent Skill.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in reference to sanity-check his own subagent/hook structure rather than reinventing harness conventions solo.
items.tryThis: Add DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices as a skill and diff its recommendations against your current subagent/hook setup.

items.title: Stack-Cairn/LiveAgent — A fully functional AI Agent desktop client that supports Webui access and can be creatively customized and expanded!
items.tldr: LiveAgent is an open-source desktop client with a WebUI for running and customizing AI agents.
items.whyItMatters: Could serve as a lightweight self-hosted control panel for checking on or steering agents from another device.
items.tryThis: Try Stack-Cairn/LiveAgent's WebUI as a remote dashboard for monitoring agent runs away from your main machine.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an agent-driven pipeline that finds, verifies, and writes reports for CVEs in source code.
items.whyItMatters: Could slot in as an automated security-verification pass before an overnight agent's PR is handed to you for morning review.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and run it against your repo's diff as a pre-merge check.

items.title: ongridio/ongrid — An ops AI Agent that understands your infrastructure, finds the root cause, and fixes it — right from Slack, Telegram, Lark or DingTalk.
items.tldr: ongrid is an ops AI agent that diagnoses and fixes infrastructure issues, controllable from Slack, Telegram, Lark or DingTalk.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you chat-based remote control for infra firefighting so you're not tethered to a laptop when something breaks off-hours.
items.tryThis: Deploy ongrid and wire it to Slack or Telegram to triage infra incidents remotely.

items.title: The Warp Agent CLI
items.tldr: Warp's Agent CLI is being discussed on HN as a terminal-native autonomous coding agent.
items.whyItMatters: Another unattended-capable coding CLI worth benchmarking against your Claude Code + worktrees/subagents setup.
items.tryThis: Run Warp Agent CLI on a side project and compare its autonomy and PR output against your current Claude Code workflow.

items.title: Oracle Just Halved Its Always Free ARM Limits
items.tldr: Oracle cut its Always Free tier ARM compute limits in half.
items.whyItMatters: If you self-host local model inference or agent sandboxes on Oracle's free ARM VMs, your free capacity just shrank.
items.tryThis: Check your OCI Always Free ARM allocation now and plan a migration or paid bump if you're near the new cap.

items.title: not much happened today
items.tldr: Roundup: Mistral's Shieldstral (3B, on-device moderation) and DeepGrove's Maple-Preview (20B ternary-weight reasoning model tuned for Mac Mini M4) lead a wave of small open-weight releases alongside Pokee-Isaac 28B (10M context, single-GPU).
items.whyItMatters: Shieldstral and Maple-Preview are small/quantized enough to run locally, giving free options for a background-tier model instead of paying API rates.
items.tryThis: Pull Shieldstral or Maple-Preview weights and try one as your local/background-tier model in a router setup.

clusters.title: Think/act/prove verification for Claude Code
clusters.summary: Two separate repos this cycle package the same completion-evidence-verification workflow so an agent (Opus or otherwise) proves its work before calling a task done.

clusters.title: Maple-Preview on-device model
clusters.summary: The same ternary 20B MoE model shows up as both a raw iPhone inference demo and part of a small-open-weights roundup tuning it for Mac Mini M4.

clusters.title: Simon Willison's LLM CLI stack update
clusters.summary: LLM 0.32 and its llm-anthropic 0.26 plugin shipped together, adding reasoning traces, a unified server-side tool interface, and new Claude model IDs.
